subject: forge-expectancy installed -- and the one decision that makes or breaks it
body:
Wrote the agent for item 1. It is installed as forge-expectancy and the file is in files/from-agent alongside EDGE.md.

There is one design decision in it that decides whether the whole thing works, so I want to say it plainly rather than bury it in a document.

OPTIMISE THE LOWER BOUND OF EXPECTANCY, NEVER THE BEST GUESS.

If we search thousands of combinations and rank them by their measured expectancy, we will not find the best process -- we will find the luckiest sample, essentially every time. That is not a refinement, it is the difference between this agent working and it being an expensive machine for fooling ourselves. So the ranking key is always expectancy minus its own uncertainty. A magnificent-looking result with a thin sample automatically loses to a modest one with a real sample, with no special rule, and that behaviour must never be tuned away when it rejects something attractive.

That single choice is how your point about live future uncertainty gets built into the objective rather than bolted on afterwards.

Four other things it fixes:

It maximises expectancy per unit of TIME, not per trade. Money compounds in time. A setup with better numbers per trade but a third of the frequency is worse, and a per-trade objective is blind to that.

It chooses the weights and the exit brackets TOGETHER. Right now the system picks the weights in one phase and the exits in a later one, but those numbers sit on a single curve -- widen the target and the win rate falls, tighten the stop and it falls faster. Choosing them separately is the bug.

It pays for its own search while searching. Every extra combination tried raises the bar the winner has to clear. We already have the machinery; a search that improves only by trying more things has found nothing, and the rising bar is what says so.

And it arms per regime on expectancy instead of on a pooled win rate. A pooled rate averages the good moments in with everything else, which is the exact operation that destroys a selective edge. The right test already exists in our code -- we use it at the end to reject regimes instead of at the front to choose them.

Then the part you asked for specifically: a plan to get good before live. Six stages, each with a pass bar and a stop condition, and no stage may be skipped or softened. In-sample sweep, purged walk-forward, combinatorial paths, an untouched holdout used exactly once, the pre-registered forward period, and only then live at reduced size.

And it says in advance what would prove it wrong: if the best jointly-chosen setup still cannot clear zero on held-out data after paying for the search, then geometry cannot save this, and the answer is different components or a different timeframe -- not another reinterpretation of the same numbers.

Say the word and I will start on it. The first thing it should do is the regime gate, because a correct objective sitting behind a pooled gate is still a pooled system.
